reasons: The rule's walk-away trigger is correctly identified: original p0133 is a no-hire ('not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire') covering 'any employee of the other party' with no general-advertising carve-out, so the deviation status is accurate.

The redline lands squarely on the playbook fallback: mutual non-solicit only, scope limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months measured from the end of the individual's involvement, and express carve-outs for general advertisements/recruitment campaigns and unsolicited approaches; the no-hire language is deleted.

Mutuality is preserved ('neither party shall, and neither party shall permit its affiliates to'), so the edit does not create a one-sided obligation, and it is directionally favorable to the Customer.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.748 changed-character ratio) is justified here — converting a no-hire into a narrowed non-solicit with new carve-outs necessarily requires rewriting the sentence; no smaller edit would remove the hire prohibition and add the carve-out.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, cites the preferred position (no non-solicit) and accepts the fallback.
